Topic: The Fundamental Bridge: The Relationship Between Integrals and Derivatives

Target audience: University students (Calculus I)

Section: section_1 — Intuitive Hook: The Velocity-Position Analogy

Lecture lines:
Imagine a squirrel gathering nuts daily.
Velocity describes how fast it travels.
The integral tracks total distance.
These are inverse operations.
Like unwrapping a gift, we reverse.

Planned animations:
Create a Dot moving linearly across the screen representing velocity. Color: #FFD700.
Display a MathTex 'v = dx/dt' near the dot. Color: #FFFFFF.
Flash the dot to emphasize constant velocity. Color: #FF4500.

Section: section_2 — Visualizing the Derivative: The Slope Tool

Lecture lines:
A derivative is a magnifying glass.
It focuses on slope at one point.
Watch the tangent line move across.

Planned animations:
Draw a tangent line touching a curve at point (x, f(x)). Color: #00BFFF.
Display MathTex 'f\'(x) = lim_{h->0}...' to define the slope. Color: #FFFFFF.
Animate the tangent line sliding along the curve to show changing slope. Color: #00BFFF.

Section: section_3 — Visualizing the Integral: The Accumulator

Lecture lines:
The integral is like a painter.
It accumulates area under the curve.
A bar sweeps, tracking the total.

Planned animations:
Create a shaded region under a curve from a to b. Color: #32CD32.
Display MathTex 'A = integral_a^b f(x) dx'. Color: #FFFFFF.
Show vertical bars filling the area progressively. Color: #32CD32.

Section: section_4 — The Fundamental Theorem: Connecting the Two

Lecture lines:
Integrating f of x gives F.
Differentiating F returns the original f.
They form a mathematical loop.
Integration reverses the differentiation process.
This is our Fundamental Theorem.

Planned animations:
Display both the curve and the area simultaneously. Colors: #00BFFF, #32CD32.
Animate the area growing as the upper limit changes. Color: #32CD32.
Flash the relationship equation 'F\'(x) = f(x)'. Color: #FFD700.

Section: section_5 — Synthesis & Summary

Lecture lines:
Integration reverses differentiation.
They are inverse mathematical processes.
Switch perspectives to solve problems.

Planned animations:
Display summary text listing Derivative vs Integral. Colors: #00BFFF, #32CD32.
Show an arrow connecting the two concepts. Color: #FFFFFF.
Fade all elements out sequentially. Color: #FFFFFF.

        # BASE

        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")

        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)

        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

            for j, col in enumerate(cols):

                y = 2.2 - i * 1

        return mobject

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
